guidance: Read the project's specification, agent instructions, README and build targets. Preserve its board configuration, dependency pins, macros and evidence.
Use the active compiler's guide and command --help. Get only the topic needed; the guide is bundled with this CLI and does not inspect or modify the project.
Find reusable definitions in the project's declared dependencies. CopperLib is one library provider; other repositories use the same interface.
Inspect selected interfaces, requirements, source notes and dependencies. Follow omissions and inherited/imported contracts before integrating a definition.
Compose board-specific intent in .copper source. Keep reusable definitions in library repositories and algorithms in CopperScript.

Run electrical checks, then the project's standard build/review workflow. Read compact routing summaries; retrieve detailed evidence for blockers. Routing closure, verified intent and hardware qualification are separate results.
For routing or placement failures, follow topic iteration: copper issues and copper view replace one-off render, inspect and codec scripts.
content.title: Start here

guidance: A .copper file declares one board, module, part, device, board_profile or macro. A board composes components/modules, nets, supplies, interfaces and physical constraints.

A board may hold one build { ... } block with defaults for the physical commands: fab_profile, and the groups placement, routing, planes and router (for example build { fab_profile = "jlcpcb-four-layer"; placement { candidates = 2; } routing { effort = balanced; } }). A command line option overrides the block. See the language reference for every key.

Board silkscreen blocks declare text, logo and shapes. The Cu logo and compiler version are included by default; opt out with silkscreen { branding { enabled = false; } }. Review final artwork placement and native DRC.

Artwork can opt into material = copper on its front/back side; exposed = true adds a matching mask opening. Branding layout = stacked puts compact name/version labels below the logo. Floating artwork reserves placement/routing space and has no electrical net. Copper glyph, filled-feature and exposed-mask qualification remain unsupported signoff checks.
Import with: import sensor "PROVIDER/PACKAGE"; component U1: sensor.Part; module SUPPORT: sensor.Support;. Use the actual exported kind and names returned by library inspection.

A net connects named endpoints: net VDD { U1.VDD; C1.1; }. A pin pattern U1.GND* names every pin of U1's part that starts with GND. Module ports become instance endpoints in the host. Inspect pin/port names and voltage/direction limits; do not infer them from footprints.
Declare pins left open on purpose: no_connect U1.PA0, U1.PA1 { reason = "unused GPIO"; }. check warns (UNMARKED_PIN) about pins that are neither connected nor declared.
Versions and replacements live in copper.mod; copper.lock binds consumed assets. Cross-library requirements must be declared in the host manifest. Source imports do not select versions.

Import a physical macro with import layout "PROVIDER/assets/layout.json"; bind existing circuitry with physical_macro NAME: layout on MODULE { member ROLE = COMPONENT; net ROLE = port.PORT; }. Omit on for board-relative mappings. Asset hashes come from copper.lock; electrical checks leave geometry pending.

Author exact physical geometry in macro NAME { ... }; import its package normally and bind physical_macro NAME: alias.Definition { ... }. Footprint imports name exact .kicad_mod assets. copper compile-macro SOURCE -o ASSET.json emits the compatible generated asset; source/footprint hashes are automatic and qualification remains separate.

Source quantities attach units (100nF, 3.3V, 0.25mm). Display engineering values with spaces and exact fixed-point fractions. Physical intent uses constraint KIND(TARGETS) { PARAMETERS; }; choose source-backed limits.
Pin-associated bypasses use role = decoupling; decouples = "U.PIN"; on the capacitor. Apply this to bypasses, not every capacitor.
The following builtin resistor divider demonstrates electrical syntax only; it is not a layout or an orderable component selection.
content.title: Language essentials

guidance: Search resolves providers declared in the consuming project's copper.mod. All query terms must match; --kind and repeatable --provider narrow results. Same-name definitions retain separate provider/package identities.

Select PACKAGE::SYMBOL from search, then pass its content_digest through --expect-digest when inspecting. Inspection reads the selected definition; inherited device and imported contracts need separate retrieval.

Start with overview, then retrieve requirements, notes and dependencies. Other sections are interfaces, properties, composition, declarations and source. Properties carry available evidence locators; external qualification files still require direct inspection.
Use repeatable --member NAME for exact declared names, component refs, constraint kinds or targets. Check unmatched_members and unselected; member selection does not remove host obligations.

Follow next_offset for omitted records. Default search is five records, inspection 20, with an 8000-character compact JSON budget. --limit, --offset and --max-chars control retrieval. needs_source means a record was too large: read its bound source or increase the budget.

Discovery is locked/offline by default. --update-lock explicitly permits lock changes; --fetch permits cache downloads. Source-derived metadata and index snapshots are descriptive, not reviewed or electrical pass certificates.
content.title: Selective library context

guidance: copper build runs check, route-board, a saved native refill with DRC and a completion gate into a fresh directory below build/, and writes run.json binding the outputs by SHA-256; it prints its step plan first, and --dry-run stops there. Options after -- go to route-board and override the board's build block, which supplies route-board's other defaults; output, report, verification and resolution options are set by the build. --verify kicad uses kicad-cli instead of the native refill and DRC.

Use the project's documented build/review target: it carries layer count, fabrication profile, footprints, placement intent, macros and native tool settings. Retain locked inputs. A generic command below needs those project options before use.

Run check for ERC and audit-footprints for selected footprint geometry before routing. Use the shared route-board pipeline and a bounded routing profile for solver work. Save reports and candidates in a fresh build directory.

route-board emits a compact summary and a source-bound requirement ledger. Default success means its routing gates passed; --require-verified-intent additionally requires hard declaration coverage. Inspect blocked, failed, assumed, external and not-run results explicitly.

Native fill evidence must match the final exported board. Use the configured KiCad executable through --verify-plane-fill and retain the generated evidence. Explicit DRC and native-filled connectivity may differ for deferred zones; the summary reports reconciled observations without altering raw findings.

Use summarize for retained route/layout reports and read full evidence only for unresolved issues. Measured length/via costs describe geometry; unsupported electrical verifiers remain blocked. Native DRC, ERC and Gerbers do not establish hardware functionality or production approval.
content.title: Build and interpret evidence

guidance: Start every failed run with copper issues RUN: findings grouped by cause, each with an id, nets, layers and a mm window. Read copper issues RUN --issue ID --json for bounded solver details, search stop reasons, unresolved pad accesses and rejected-trial provenance. Rejected candidates are not retained-board DRC findings. Fix root causes first. Advisory X ids come from the placed board's escape model: nets between two parts that cross on one layer, or inner pins of a pad field with too few ring gaps. M ids (stage emi) are EMI screening estimates from the report's emi section, not EMC qualification; copper emi-check BOARD --run RUN --write adds the section to an older run. Filter with --stage, --net or --code.

Look at one issue with copper view RUN --issue ID (add --filled to select saved native zone fills). Read the printed legend first; open the SVG when geometry matters. Saved fills are translucent; unfilled zones are dashed outlines. The viewer does not refill or show rule-area keepouts. Use --net, --pad, --component or --window x0,y0,x1,y1 for anything else.

For a blocked package exit, overlay the manufacturer layout: copper view RUN --issue R1 --reference REF.kicad_pcb --align OURS:THEIRS. The legend states matched pads and fit RMS; an overlay is a comparison aid, not proof that the reference applies.

Do not read route-report.json whole or write per-failure render, plot, inspect or codec scripts. If a script is unavoidable, build it on the copper CLI (copper issues, copper view, copper state show) and keep intermediate solver states with route-board --checkpoint-dir.

When solver internals are needed, add a reusable, tested diagnostic to CopperScript instead of monkeypatching private functions in a one-off script. Repair details distinguish the target search from the restoration search; rejected restoration geometry is not retained-board DRC.

Read retained per-net copper metrics, including compliant nets and replay-unified results, with copper summarize REPORT --net NET --json. Replays retain physical DRC findings and routing_quality; they do not acquire native verification or engineering approval. Copper length does not prove connectivity, and explicit-copper connectivity does not certify native filled-plane connectivity. Missing legacy metrics remain unavailable.

Do not rerun the whole pipeline to test an early fix. route-board --stop-after placement ends after placement and global routing (the report is marked stopped_after and is never signoff). Add --checkpoint-dir DIR to save placement, then --reuse-placement DIR/placement.state.json to skip placement and global routing while changing later stages; reuse is refused when the board or placement options changed. A failed run with --report leaves route-report.error.json (open stage with --progress, named components), listed by copper issues.

Change generic algorithms or source intent, rerun the project's standard target into a fresh directory, and compare issue counts. Grouped issues and views are reading aids: report gates, native checks and qualification remain authoritative.
content.title: Iterate on routing and placement failures

guidance: If this compiler lacks agent-guide or library commands, inspect its --help and the project's compiler pin. Select a current compiler explicitly for guidance/review using the project's documented workflow; retain existing build pins.

On a missing lock/cache, inspect copper.mod and the resolver diagnostic. Use the documented dependency setup. Explicit --fetch or --update-lock are available for library discovery when the task calls for fetching or changing dependencies; do not treat a checksum mismatch as permission to update.

On empty search, check query terms, provider and kind. Search covers declared dependencies. A missing dependency or unsupported host needs manifest/setup work; it is not proof that no suitable part exists.

On stale --expect-digest, repeat selection against current resolved content. On duplicate exports, repair the library. On omissions or needs_source, retrieve the indicated page or exact source before treating an obligation as understood.

On check failures, run copper check --json: findings carry file/line/column, hints and machine-applicable fixes; copper explain CODE gives the usual cause and fix. Use copper query BOARD pins|net|unconnected to verify intent instead of re-reading source.

On ERC, routing, native or requirement failures, use the compact issue's source origin and detailed report. Preserve exact pins, limits, immutable macro copper and required via arrays. Reproduce solver failures in a small shared fixture; report unsupported checks as incomplete.
content.title: Recover with bounded context
Simulate benches
guidance: A bench (bench NAME for BOARD { ... }) lives in benches/*.copper beside the board file. It adds sources, loads and simulation-only components, replaces or ignores board components, names one analysis (ac, dc, loop, noise, op, pz or tran; several as sections, analysis NAME: KIND { ... }), steps params, and declares let, measure and plot expressions; the language reference's Simulation section has the syntax.

Setup that several benches share goes in a fixture NAME for TARGET { ... } file in benches/ (supplies, models, replace, ignore, params, bench components and nets); a bench names it with bench NAME for TARGET using FIXTURE { ... } and overrides a fixture param, supply, model, replace or component by declaring the same name. A limit that applies to some steps only takes where: measure m = ... { max = 1%; where R_SOIL <= 100ohm; }, so one bench holds rated and stress conditions; limits may also name params.

analysis noise { from; to; points_per_decade; output = V(OUT); input = SRC; } gives noise() (output density), noise(X) (one component's or bench model's part), input_noise() and noise_rms(x, from, to) / noise_share(x, from, to) over a band. Components declare tolerance = 1%; and matched networks match = "NAME"; match_tolerance = 0.01%;; a bench adds tolerance TARGET = q; (params, passives, COMPONENT.PARAMETER) and runs montecarlo { runs = 200; seed = 1; } or worstcase; over them, with every limit applied to the worst run.

analysis tran { stop = 2ms; start; max_step; reltol; } runs in time; a source takes waveform = sine | pulse | pwl | step { ... }; (dc and ac stay its op and ac values). Parts may declare sim diode { anode; cathode; ... } and sim switch { a; b; ctrl; ctrl_ref; ... }; op-amps clip at their rails less output_swing_from_*_rail, slew at slew_rate and limit output_current_limit in tran runs only. Measures over time: min max mean rms pp (also over a window, max(x, 1ms, 2ms); in ac the window is a sub-band, max(mag(h), 1kHz, 10kHz)), at(x, t), cross(x, level), settle(x, band), overshoot(x), harmonic(x, f0, n), thd(x, f0) (thd(x, f0, n) to harmonic n), integrate(x). Bandwidths: upto(db(h) > -3dB) is the frequency up to which the comparison holds from the start of the sweep, downto(...) from its end. A tran run starts from ic V(NODE) = q;, ic C1 = q; and ic L1 = q; (held during the operating point), or with uic = true; from the capacitor voltages and inductor currents alone.

analysis dc { sweep = SOURCE_OR_PARAM; from = -4V; to = 4V; step = 0.1V; } solves operating points over a source's dc, a supply's voltage or a param, with continuation and the op-amp clipping and current limit active (a transfer curve clips at the rails); probes are real over the swept value: at(x, 1V), cross, upto, max. I(X) and I(X.ROLE) of a replaced component or bench model read the current into the model's terminals.

Stability: analysis loop { from; to; points_per_decade; probe = U1.OUT; } reads the loop gain at a component pin through a 0 V probe in series with it (Tian's method; the operating point unchanged, other loops closed): loop_gain() is complex over frequency, and phase_margin(T), gain_margin(T), crossover(T), phase_crossover(T) are its margins (never without a crossing). Probe an amplifier's output pin, a one-way break; a pin between two loops gives a loop gain that is not one loop's. analysis pz; gives the poles of the linearised circuit (with input = SRC; output = V(OUT); also the zeros) and the built-in measure stable, which fails on a pole in the right half-plane; damping() is the smallest damping ratio. The text table names the nodes each worrying pole dominates.

Supply current: an opamp or diffamp block with quiescent_current = 19mA; draws it into vp and out of vn, and the current its output delivers from the rail that sources it, in every analysis, so I(SUPPLY), I(U1.VP) and I(U1.VN) read real rail currents (without it the supply pins carry none, as before); each such rail needs a DC path to ground (SIM102). psrr = 80dB; (psrr_corner = 10kHz;) adds the input-referred error (V(vp) - V(vn) - span) / PSRR, span the DC rail span the bench sets, so a rail tone or a dc sweep of a supply reaches the output. A rail with impedance is a supply replaced with (or a module port driven by) a source with output_resistance; the board's decoupling capacitors then act. sim spice subcircuits draw whatever rail current their netlist has. A rail can come from its regulator instead: model NAME: regulator { in; out; gnd; en; output_voltage = 4.5V; dropout = 0.26V; soft_start = 14ms; enable_threshold = 2.1V; quiescent_current = 49uA; } (also output_resistance, output_impedance_corner, psrr, psrr_corner, output_current_limit, voltage_noise; efficiency = 85%; makes it an averaged DC-DC converter, input power = output power / efficiency, no switching ripple) or sim reference (startup_time instead of soft_start), in every analysis; I(X.in), I(X.out), I(X.gnd) read its terminals, and its out counts as set to output_voltage for parameter sets per supply and psrr spans. An adjustable part is a bench model at the set point of its divider; a psrr on a rail model needs its input set by a supply, source or rail model (SIM104); block checks are SIM103.

bench NAME for MODULE { ... } simulates one module of the board on its own (its local component and net names, its ports as nets), so it needs no ignore list for the rest of the board: the bench supplies the ports with supply NAME { voltage = q; net = PORT; } (one at 0 V is the ground) and model NAME: source { out = PORT; ref = GND; ... } for signal sources. Prefer a module bench to a board bench full of ignores.

copper sim BOARD runs every bench (--bench NAME runs one): the analysis once per combination of step values. It prints each measure's worst step against its limits and writes sim-results.json (copperscript-sim/v0.1), BENCH.csv and BENCH.html (plots and the measures table) in --out (default build/sim). Exit status 1 means a measure is outside its limits or a bench cannot be solved; 2 a usage or compile error.

Every component is modelled (a passive by its value, a part by its sim block), replaced or ignored; the results name each component's fidelity (ideal, macro, vendor, replaced, ignored). A part's sim spice { file = "models/amp.lib"; subckt = "AMP"; dialect = pspice; terminals = INP, INN, VP, VN, OUT; } runs a SPICE subcircuit read natively (fidelity vendor); a vendor model is source = "https://..."; sha256 = "..."; (member = "x.lib" inside a ZIP), never committed: copper models fetch BOARD caches it, copper sim never downloads (SIM077), params = values { GAIN = 10; }; overrides the subcircuit's PARAMS: defaults (SIM105), and a construct the reader does not support is SIM078 with file, line and element (MOSFET levels 1 and 3 with Meyer gate charge, lossless T lines, DELAY(), DDT() and LAPLACE exp(-s T) are read; BSIM, VDMOS, lossy lines and SDT are not). Macro models are built-in parameter models, not vendor models; their swing and current limit act in tran runs and dc sweeps, their slew rate in tran runs, not in ac, op or noise runs, and their noise densities only noise runs; unused ones are listed as inactive.

A part may carry a macro and a vendor model for one unit: a built-in block (sim opamp, sim regulator, ...) and a sim spice block with the same unit (or both without one). copper sim runs the macro model; --models vendor runs the sim spice model where a unit has one (its file must be cached), --models macro only built-in models (a part with only a sim spice model is SIM107). Each choice must cover every pin on its own (SIM106). A vendor file that cannot be fetched by a script (analog.com) is declared sim spice { sha256 = "..."; download = "where to get it"; subckt; terminals; }: download it by hand and run copper models add BOARD FILE, which checks the hash and copies it into .copper-cache/spice/<sha256>/ (a file no part declares is refused, with its SHA-256 and .SUBCKT lines printed); missing, it is SIM108 naming the download note. Vendor files live in the cache of the board's project, also for parts from a library package.

copper sim --check-model PART BOARD runs a standard bench set on a part of the board's library instead of the benches: amplifiers at --supply (default 10 V as +/-5 V) get supply current, open-loop gain, gain-bandwidth (at G = 100), phase margin, follower bandwidth, voltage noise and slew rate; regulators and references quiescent current, output voltage, output resistance, line rejection, dropout, efficiency, output noise and start-up. The macro figures are judged against the values the block declares within the printed tolerances; the vendor figures are printed beside them with the difference (DIFFERS beyond 25 % or 3 dB). It passes when the models load, the operating points converge and every judged figure holds; a vendor file not in the cache is reported and leaves the verdict to the macro model. --tie PIN=vn ties a subcircuit pin the macro block leaves unmodelled (an OPA547's ILIM); --no-tran or --tran-budget SECONDS bound the slow vendor transients. SIM109 when a part cannot be checked.

A failing measure is a finding about the circuit or the bench: read the plots and the per-step table before changing anything, and never loosen a limit or a model value to make a bench pass. A solver error names the floating net and the component pins on it, or the loop of voltage sources.
